children: Argentina's wheat harvest for the 2026/27 season is expected to total 23.8 million metric tons, up from the 21 million estimated last month, due to higher-than-expected yields, the Rosario Stock Exchange said on Wednesday.
If achieved, the figure would mark the second-largest wheat harvest on record for Argentina, a key global food exporter.
Santa Fe province expects yields approaching 4 tons per hectare, slightly surpassing Buenos Aires, Argentina's traditional wheat-growing region.
Below-normal temperatures for early spring are benefiting crop development, though concerns exist about limited sunny days.
Argentina's wheat harvest begins in November.
The exchange kept its soybean and corn forecasts unchanged for 2026/27 at 47.8 million and 67.5 million tons, respectively.
